newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Sri Lanka Army pours men and material into its fifty-fifth division, which launched operation Jaya Sikuru recently to reopen a strategic highway linking the north with the rest of the country, security sources say. The northern Jaffna peninsula, which the military recaptured from Tamil separatists (LTTE) in 1996, is now supplied by air and sea.

Politicl parties in parliament must agree on framework within which a solution to the northeast conflict could be discussed with the LTTE, before the government considers opening talks with rebels, says Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister, G.L. Peiris.

Crew of North Korean merchant ship Morang Bong say they will not leave Sri Lanka until LTTE release their vessel. The rebels captured the ship last week off the northern Point Pedro coast, when one of its 38 crewmen was killed in a shootout and the rest were released through the ICRC.
Police arrest a 43-year-old Tamil woman who has supplied LTTE with information from Colombo for six years, security sources say.
